import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Melt the data to create a pivot table for seaborn bar plot
df_melted = pd.melt(df, id_vars=['sex'], value_vars=['pclass', 'sibsp', 'parch', 'fare'], var_name='Attribute', value_name='Value')

# Create the bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='Attribute', y='Value', hue='sex', data=df_melted)

# Set the title and labels
plt.title('Average Values of Passenger Attributes by Sex')
plt.xlabel('Attribute')
plt.ylabel('Average Value')
plt.legend(title='Sex')

# Rotate the x-axis labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the plot to a file

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Melt the data to create a pivot table for seaborn bar plot
df_melted = pd.melt(df, id_vars=['sex'], value_vars=['pclass', 'sibsp', 'parch', 'fare'], var_name='Attribute', value_name='Value')

# Create the bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='Attribute', y='Value', hue='sex', data=df_melted)

# Set the title and labels
plt.title('Average Values of Passenger Attributes by Sex')
plt.xlabel('Attribute')
plt.ylabel('Average Value')
plt.legend(title='Sex')

# Rotate the x-axis labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
